payload.summary: Session 1 (first). No founder-ledger.jsonl, /work/referee empty (no result.json, no control.json readable): no referee verdict exists for this brain. spec/asama-0 is not frozen, so this session's single job is the stage 0 spec request (29b push types).

Read 00-ozet and all of spec/asama-0 against the tohum/02 structural list: 8 sections present; every #id of the 3 declared capabilities heads a row in 10/10a; thresholds keyed to policy.json or seed rules; budget 246 USD under the 300 USD proposal; each MF is one tool (04); 21 MF tests map 1:1 between 0.9 and 0.14; calls order holds; no target-specific name; page line counts match. No correction needed, so the push only appends a dated review line to spec/asama-0/CHANGELOG.md, plus this ledger and reports/.

[seed_issue] seed-001-seed-dir-missing: missing_capability: the brain repo has no seed/ tree (git ls-files at HEAD lists only spec/). 24a:50 places seed/** (bootstrap, drill, launcher) in the brain repo; 00a:25-26 and 26:18 require the founder ledger to be appended with the seed tool `founder-ledger append`; asama-0/09:12 and asama-0/14:51-53 name seed/bootstrap/stages/stage0.json as the machine copy. The Founder can run neither. Rows in this ledger are written with the Founder's own RFC 8785 + sha256 implementation, checked against 29a V1 and V2 (both match).

After the 2.2 narrowing asama-0/10:29 says spec.lint and gate.lock are not called in (A), asama-0/13:36-38 lists them as absent in stage 0, 00a:76 and asama-0/14 have 18 MFs. If the referee follows 29b, exit (A) cannot pass.

The 27 reader table (lines 50-67) and 27a have no row for tests/fixtures/toy-repo/ (readers would be import, #oyuncak toy_tree_sha256, #agac). The mechanical #okuyucu check can fail on this seed omission.

[spec_issue] spec-004-calls-17-18: '17 ve 18 hepsini cagirir' is ambiguous: the order rule (asama-0/14:20-21; 26c: each called MF is smaller than its caller) forbids 17 calling 18, yet 'hepsini' reads as all MFs. Should read 'kendilerinden onceki hepsini'. Not edited: asama-0/14:53 requires 14, 0.9 and stage0.json to change in one seed epoch, and stage0.json is seed.

[seed_issue] seed-005-push-class-ledger: 29b:36 defines a spec request as a push changing only spec/asama-*/ and spec/INDEX.md; 29b:41 rejects pushes mixing spec and code. 00a:25-27 and 26:18 require each session from the first to append founder-ledger.jsonl, and reports go to reports/. This first-session push carries the spec review plus ledger and reports; its class depends on that unwritten rule.

MF1 built: referee/ledger/chain.py (RFC 8785 with keys in UTF-16 order, integers only per tohum/26, duplicate keys/NaN/lone surrogates/deep nesting refused; row_hash = sha256(canonical(row - row_hash) || prev_hash); verify checks link, own hash, and with --previous byte-identical prefix). Test 13 = referee/tests/test_chain.py, 22 tests / 43 cases, all through the CLI in a subprocess from referee/, files via /dev/fd pipes so it runs in a read-only container. V1 -> 3bae9158..., V2 -> 3b10a5bb..., V3 -> broken r2 line 2; founder-ledger.jsonl verifies. Deliberate breakage: 12 mutants (plain code-point sort, prev_hash left out of hash, row_hash kept in body, link check off, hash check off, --previous ignored, prefix length-only, floats allowed, duplicate keys allowed, control chars unescaped, upper-case hex, recursion guard removed) each turn the suite red; deleting ledger/chain.py turns all 43 cases red. snowball-tests.json: T13, done_mf [1].

Interface choices where 29a:70-71 is silent: verify exits 0 valid, 1 broken, 2 unusable input (missing file, usage), always one JSON line {valid, broken_row, line, reason}; broken_row is the row_id or 'line:N' when the line has none; hash refuses (exit 2, {error}) more or fewer than one line, a bad prev_hash, and floats. Floats are refused rather than serialised the ECMAScript way because tohum/26:31-33 bans floating point in hashed artifacts, so a float row is a broken row. A row re-serialised with different whitespace is a valid chain but not append-only (byte prefix), because the file, not its parse, is what was published.

[seed_issue] seed-007-chain-cli-exit-and-broken-row: 29a:70-71 gives verify's output as {valid, broken_row} but not the exit code for a broken chain nor the broken_row value for a line with no row_id; 29d:92-100 says the generic runner compares the stdout JSON and treats only exit 125 as runner_fault. If the seed's runner treats exit 1 as a failed command, V3 (a correctly reported broken chain) would be red. The Founder's chain exits 1 on a broken chain and names such lines 'line:N'.

Interface choices where 26a, 29a and 29d are silent: python -m gate.secrets scan --kind diff|row|prompt [--known-env NAME] [FILE|stdin] prints {clean, kind, run_valid, matches}; send [--known-env NAME] -- CMD runs CMD with the prompt on stdin only when it is clean and prints {clean, run_valid, sent, sender_exit, matches}; exit 0 clean, 1 match, 2 unusable input (never clean). A match is {rule, line, sha256[, path]}: no value, per 30c:10-11. Each line is scanned raw, with \uXXXX/\xNN decoded, and NFKC-folded without format characters; a whole diff is scanned, removed lines included, since a diff in a prompt leaks either way. Library: scan, require_clean (raises SecretFound), send_if_clean, for llm.call, gate.check and ledger.append later.

MF2 built: referee/gate/secrets.py (15 token rules plus a quoted secret-named assignment with an entropy check, known values from named env vars, three spellings per line, fail-closed decoding). Covers every rule in diff, row and prompt, one-changed-byte inputs clean, escaped/zero-width/full-width spellings, removed diff lines and path, known env values, send never starting the sender on a match, unusable input exit 2, and the real ledger and this push scanning clean. Deliberate breakage: 15 mutants (raw-only, no path, send despite match, value leaked, exit 0 on match, added lines only, no assignment rule, no minimum known length, everything random, strict UTF-8, fail open, jwt rule off, no fold, no URL placeholder list, line off by one) each turn it red; deleting gate/secrets.py turns it red (19 failures, 49 errors). gate/secrets.py: one assignment rule for quoted and bare values of 8+ chars after a secret-named key (pwd and credential added); _placeholder replaces the entropy check; a bare value drops a sentence-ending full stop or colon. Same class found while testing: in a JSON row the quotes around a value are escaped, so a quoted secret in a ledger row scanned clean; the escape variant now also decodes backslash-quote, slash and backslash. gate/secrets.py: the assignment value is no longer captured by a character class but read by _value: unquoted, it runs to the first whitespace outside brackets (one trailing , ; . : and unmatched closers are syntax); quoted, to the closing quote not escaped by a backslash, with an optional string prefix (f, b, r) and a glued tail. A value is skipped only when it is nothing but templates, one repeated character, a placeholder word, or (unquoted) code by an explicit recursive-descent grammar (_is_code: dotted or underscored letter names, or calls, subscripts, slices and groups over names, numbers and string literals). Same class, found by me while fixing and closed in this push: a subscripted key (config[name] = value), comparisons (== != === !==), type annotations and the Go string type, command-line flags followed by a value, an Authorization scheme word before an opaque token, an escaped quote inside a quoted value, text glued after a closing quote, and a URL password shorter than 6 characters. The two-line join for assignments now only gives a key that ends a line its value from the next line (the old join glued unrelated lines into fake annotations).
